23cWKG6LF47H1G3EfhV5dmEYtxkNaqLWgFDxEurd.text:
{"description":"Actor specialization for an action attributed directly to a principal: a person, organization, account owner, or
other primary authority recognized by the event source. A Principal Actor means the provider is asserting that the
action was performed under the principal's own authority, not by a delegated agent acting independently on the
principal's behalf.

This type does not specify how the provider authenticated the principal. A concrete subtype can describe a browser
session, biometric challenge, API credential treated as direct principal control, hardware key, bank login, or
government identity proof. The important invariant is semantic attribution: when a Blue document asks whether an
operation was performed by a principal, a Principal Actor or compatible subtype is the category it is checking.

Principal Actor also does not automatically authorize every operation. A document may still require a particular
source, stronger authentication, a specific account, a particular organization role, or additional domain-specific
conditions. This type supplies the actor category used by those policies.
","name":"Principal Actor","type":{"blueId":"GnMntk3hLvHEsZTBE8Gk7ytPBexj6jhBJHdaxnJYhEQ7"}}

299jVUofgxbkqW1JY3zxHjc4ivtdUPsNns5ow8dT.text: {"adjustmentRatio":{"description":"The number that denotes the cumulative quantity of post-split shares issued to shareholders versus the quantity of pre-split shares previously issued to shareholders.  This number will be multiplied by existing shares in an equity derivative contract or other positions to determine the post-split number of shares.  With regard to any reference to price, the pre-split reference price will be divided by this number to determine the post-split reference price.\n","schema":{"required":{"type":{"blueId":"AwvXD961fmnmqcSQhjMA7r15HpVh39cefb6ZTyUz2Fm2"},"value":true}},"type":{"blueId":"9eWaHYz2vKrFofdHTHAizNNu8xP6QE3WQ5y7DGrGZvyJ"}},"description":"Data required to perform a stock split business event.","effectiveDate":{"description":"The effective date of the stock split, also known as the ex-date. This is the date on which the additional shares are paid to the shareholders, or in the case of a reverse stock split, the number shares held by each shareholder is proportionally reduced.  Equity derivative transactions can be amended in firms' internal systems on such date.   In most markets, the listed stock price is reduced (or increased for a reverse stock split) to account for the split on the same date, but in some markets the price adjustment occurs on a later date.  In either case, equity derivative transactions should be amended on the date that the stocks are paid to the shareholders (or consolidated).\n","schema":{"required":{"type":{"blueId":"AwvXD961fmnmqcSQhjMA7r15HpVh39cefb6ZTyUz2Fm2"},"value":true}},"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"}},"name":"cdm/event/common/StockSplitInstruction"}

for contexts where the caller is already authorized to request the change and the document policy allows direct
application.

blocks forbidden `/contracts` modifications when Contracts Change Policy requires sectionChanges, rejects attempts to

","type":{"blueId":"6r7X1t4mk8pzhtyij1QDYaoMrseQxsRdHuJTw8dJaEk2"}},"dayType":{"description":"In the case of an offset specified as a number of days, this element defines whether consideration is given as to whether a day is a good business day or not. If a day type of business days is specified then non-business days are ignored when calculating the offset. The financial business centers to use for determination of business days are implied by the context in which this element is used. This element must only be included when the offset is specified as a number of days. If the offset is zero days then the dayType element should not be included.
","type":{"blueId":"7SsDfFvRbfxrm8vS98NZ5Vq9nqD3CFNGWsLr6dc738LJ"}},"description":"A class defining a date (referred to as the derived date) as a relative offset from another date (referred to as the anchor date). If the anchor date is itself an adjustable date then the offset is assumed to be calculated from the adjusted anchor date. A number of different scenarios can be supported, namely; 1) the derived date may simply be a number of calendar periods (days, weeks, months or years) preceding or following the anchor date; 2) the unadjusted derived date may be a number of calendar periods (days, weeks, months or years) preceding or following the anchor date with the resulting unadjusted derived date subject to adjustment in accordance with a specified business day convention, i.e. the derived date must fall on a good business day; 3) the derived date may be a number of business days preceding or following the anchor date. Note that the businessDayConvention specifies any required adjustment to the unadjusted derived date. A negative or positive value in the periodMultiplier indicates whether the unadjusted derived precedes or follows the anchor date. The businessDayConvention should contain a value NONE if the day type element contains a value of Business (since specifying a negative or positive business days offset would already guarantee that the derived date would fall on a good business day in the specified business centers).

{"description":"Optional static and deterministic request-validation configuration used by
Mandate documents. The containing concrete mandate type defines the input
examined by this configuration and the runtime component that invokes it.

Validation passes only when both configured checks pass: request is absent or
matches the candidate input, and function is absent or evaluates to Boolean
true for that same input.
","function":{"description":"Optional deterministic BEX validation program represented as a Blue node.
This field intentionally has no repository-local nominal BEX type: program
syntax and compilation are defined by the BEX specification and runtime.

By convention, the host passes the candidate input being validated as the
immutable BEX binding named request. Concrete mandate types define the
semantic meaning of that input.

A concrete mandate document may define function.entry to select a local
function. When present, function.functions must declare a callable function
with exactly that name. The feeder or provider invokes the selected entry
without arguments; the candidate input remains available through the
request binding.

When function is absent, function validation passes. When present, only the
Boolean result true passes. False, null, undefined, a non-Boolean result, or
deterministic compilation or execution failure rejects the candidate.
"},"name":"Mandate Validation","request":{"description":"Optional static Blue pattern matched against the input defined by the
concrete mandate type. When absent, static request-shape matching imposes
no additional restriction.

The same candidate input is passed to function as the immutable BEX binding
named request.
"}}

{"description":"Source specialization for an authenticated interactive browser, mobile, or user-interface session. Browser Session
records that the event source observed the request through an interactive session rather than a background API
credential. It is often combined with Principal Actor when a document wants evidence of direct human involvement.

Browser Session does not, by itself, guarantee a particular authentication strength. A concrete subtype may define
password login, two-factor authentication, biometric verification, hardware key challenge, regulated strong customer
authentication, or other assurance details. Documents that require those stronger conditions should check the
concrete subtype or additional fields, not merely the base Browser Session type.

A Timeline Provider or event source authenticates the session and records the source. Blue documents later use that
source attribution to decide whether a requested operation meets their policy. The provider is infrastructure: it
validates the session and appends the entry; it does not need to understand the business meaning of the message.
","name":"Browser Session","type":{"blueId":"Qm35f9xFUH84i745uPMj5jjMX1oCCG79aeSfHViipxG"},"uiSessionNonce":{"description":"Provider-generated identifier for the UI session or interaction context. It may be opaque outside the provider, but
it should be sufficient for provider-side audit, incident review, revocation, and correlation with authentication
records. It MUST NOT contain secret session credentials.
","type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"}}}

argument patterns. Definitions do not execute by themselves; a Compute step selects an entry function or imports the

{"description":"Concrete Operation handler whose implementation is an ordered Sequential Workflow. Because Operation extends Handler,
a Sequential Workflow Operation is discovered and invoked as a same-scope handler bound to its channel.

A Sequential Workflow Operation is still invoked like any other Operation: callers post an Operation Request naming
the operation contract key and its effective channel, and the request payload must conform to this operation's request
shape. The request may be accepted through a different eligible source channel. A supporting processor routes it to
the operation's effective channel while preserving source-channel checkpoint semantics. The workflow then runs the
declared steps deterministically and returns effects such as triggered events or document updates through the Blue
Contracts processor.

Use this for document-owned behavior where the operation interface and implementation should live together in a single
contract entry. A plain Operation can still declare the operation interface when a runtime or document chooses to bind
the implementation separately.
","name":"Sequential Workflow Operation","steps":{"description":"Append-only ordered workflow steps to run when this operation is invoked. The steps have the same semantics as steps
in a Sequential Workflow: Compute steps compute data, Update Document steps request processor-managed patches, and
Trigger Event steps emit Blue events. The processor remains responsible for validation, patch application, event
routing, deterministic ordering, gas, and post-patch type soundness.

The append-only merge policy preserves inherited workflow prefixes. Subtypes and concrete documents may append
additional steps, but must not replace, reorder, or positionally overlay inherited steps.
","itemType":{"blueId":"9oGn8V6FSVcJYhRfuHRShfWjiHBUqzxVi9StGtHZNfev"},"type":{"blueId":"85ip88snCGrgUNdi1rUFqqAxcxwVGKV2g4LjsKoyKmXK"}},"type":{"blueId":"7pZPbabkYt8GUuY8JnALqhJ7gqoChfZoE5tKmU3gBpFv"}}

{"description":"Marker contract that identifies a logical section of a document and links that section to the fields and contracts
responsible for it. A section gives humans, agents, and change-management workflows a coherent unit of meaning such as
payment setup, shipping details, consent terms, participant configuration, or embedded-order handling.

`title` and `summary` describe the section in user-facing terms. `relatedFields` lists absolute document pointers for
state fields covered by the section. `relatedContracts` lists same-scope contract keys that implement, enforce, or
affect the section. Section-aware workflows use this information to group proposed contract changes, validate that
contract edits belong to the right section, and present changes for review.

Document Section is metadata with runtime relevance only for workflows that understand it. It is also identity-bearing
document content. Changing a section's title, summary, fields, or related contracts changes what the document says
about its own structure and review surface.
","name":"Document Section","relatedContracts":{"description":"Contract keys in the same scope that implement or affect the section.","itemType":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"type":{"blueId":"85ip88snCGrgUNdi1rUFqqAxcxwVGKV2g4LjsKoyKmXK"}},"relatedFields":{"description":"Absolute JSON Pointer paths of fields covered by this section.","itemType":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"type":{"blueId":"85ip88snCGrgUNdi1rUFqqAxcxwVGKV2g4LjsKoyKmXK"}},"summary":{"description":"Brief functional summary of the section's purpose and behavior.","type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"}},"title":{"description":"Short, human-readable title shown in UI summaries.","type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"}},"type":{"blueId":"8nWeksYEXxp5TBnRcYF5u3VsFHvMfxo4zjAFT6MLW8ZD"}}

{"description":"Handler contract that executes an ordered list of workflow steps after its bound channel delivers an event. Sequential
Workflow is the standard coordination runtime for expressing document-owned logic without embedding host code. It
reads the channelized payload, runs each step in order, records step results under step names when applicable, and
returns processor effects such as patches, triggered events, explicit gas, or termination requests.

The workflow is sequential: later steps can read earlier step results through `$steps` and can observe prior Update
Document steps through the workflow's working document. The working document should be frozen/snapshot-backed and
advanced by the same patch, conformance, dynamic generalization, and Type Generalization Policy rules that the Blue
Contracts processor will use at commit time. This gives read-your-writes behavior without materializing the entire
document as mutable state.

Sequential Workflow does not weaken the Blue Contracts processor model. Patches are still applied through Update
Document. Events are still emitted through Trigger Event or result emission. Boundary rules, reserved-key protection,
post-patch type soundness, generalization, Document Update cascades, checkpoints, and gas accounting remain processor
responsibilities. The workflow only provides a deterministic authoring/runtime structure for arranging these steps.
","name":"Sequential Workflow","steps":{"description":"Ordered list of workflow steps. The list order is execution order. A step may expose a named result for later steps,
but actual document mutation and event routing still occur through processor-defined effect application.
","itemType":{"blueId":"9oGn8V6FSVcJYhRfuHRShfWjiHBUqzxVi9StGtHZNfev"},"type":{"blueId":"85ip88snCGrgUNdi1rUFqqAxcxwVGKV2g4LjsKoyKmXK"}},"type":{"blueId":"2Ag2NfcWpCfPqBAR7bFAEL9L3roX3UWGUkDq7nN3D4gV"}}

{"description":"Generic class to specify the quantity for different payout legs in a contractual product, when that quantity can vary across payout legs or across time. A resolvable quantity can always be resolved into a single quantity from the quantity notation which has a corresponding asset identifier. In addition to the base case, where quantity is directly specified as a number as part of the quantity notation, the other use cases are: (i) quantity based on some pre-defined schedule (eg amortising notional), (ii) quantity based on some pre-defined events (eg resetting cross-currency notional), or quantity set as reference to another quantity (eg equity notional as no. securities x price).
","futureValueNotional":{"description":"The future value notional is specific to BRL CDI swaps, and is specified alongside the notional amount. The value is calculated as follows: Future Value Notional = Notional Amount * (1 + Fixed Rate) ^ (Fixed Rate Day Count Fraction). The currency should always match that expressed in the notional schedule. The value date should match the adjusted termination date.
","type":{"blueId":"GEiYETZkL7VKU2MM1UAEcnjv6pLTquUhrhn3vWrBeUh"}},"name":"cdm/product/common/settlement/ResolvablePriceQuantity","priceSchedule":{"description":"A payout's price specified as a schedule, which may also contain a single value if that price is constant. There may be multiple prices specified for a single payout: e.g. a floating interest rate leg may specify a spread, a cap and/or floor and a multiplier. The price must be specified outside of the payout in a PriceQuantity object and only referenced inside the payout using an address.
","itemType":{"blueId":"2Uog2mdWokkHVaMVWG2ZhXCKPdQtauRk7oxemYRLn9hy"},"schema":{"minItems":{"type":{"blueId":"E2LM6qgzWG9ttagq2xTmiZkgYEAgkYedFCmU9v7NnVEq"},"value":0}},"type":{"blueId":"85ip88snCGrgUNdi1rUFqqAxcxwVGKV2g4LjsKoyKmXK"}},"quantityMultiplier":{"description":"Quantity multiplier is specified on top of a reference quantity and is used as a multiplying factor when resolving the quantity. A quantity multiplier can only exist when the resolvable quantity specifies a reference quantity.
","type":{"blueId":"FedvzuiBHcBGaUCXw7uDaxGpMKLfGio3HvCGdjqZZy2A"}},"quantityReference":{"description":"Reference quantity when resolvable quantity is defined as relative to another (resolvable) quantity. A resolvable quantity needs to contain either an absolute quantity or a reference to another (resolvable) quantity. This requirement is captured by a choice rule on the class.
","type":{"blueId":"Dyqr7TA1HN5EcvzLV8Yzj2SDcBRhKaKqVGCBXkTfUDZZ"}},"quantitySchedule":{"description":"A payout's quantity specified as a schedule, which may also contain a single value if that quantity is constant. There can only be a single quantity schedule applicable to a payout: e.g. the notional for an interest rate leg. The quantity must be specified outside of the payout in a PriceQuantity object and only referenced inside the payout using an address.
","type":{"blueId":"3QpANvMr6891ZuV6c8Yze7qcCyqbKRhy9zqwHuMkw8FP"}},"reset":{"description":"Whether the quantity is resettable","type":{"blueId":"AwvXD961fmnmqcSQhjMA7r15HpVh39cefb6ZTyUz2Fm2"}},"resolvedQuantity":{"description":"A product's quantity as a single, non-negative amount.  When specified as part of a product definition, this quantity attribute would not be set.  Instead it is specified on the quantity notation along with an asset identifier matching this payout's asset identifier.  This allows the quantity to be resolved for a payout leg, which can then be specified here for convenience during data processing.  There needs to be at least one resolvable quantity across payout legs of a product to define an anchor that other payout quantities can refer to.  This attribute is ignored when mapping existing FpML messages.
","type":{"blueId":"6H6ai9i2XAXM89wp9H6hTxLjhKaoFgBxrauHYKfRY3pL"}}}

NonTransferableProduct.description: The non-transferable product data type represents a product that can be traded (as part of a TradableProduct) but cannot be transferred to others.

TransferableProduct.description: A TransferableProduct is a type of financial product which can be held or transferred, represented as an Asset with the addition of specific EconomicTerms.

body.description: Enables either a TransferableProduct or a NonTransferableProduct to be used in an underlier.
body.name: cdm/product/template/Product

NonTransferableProduct.description: The non-transferable product data type represents a product that can be traded (as part of a TradableProduct) but cannot be transferred to others.

TransferableProduct.description: A TransferableProduct is a type of financial product which can be held or transferred, represented as an Asset with the addition of specific EconomicTerms.

members.description: Enables either a TransferableProduct or a NonTransferableProduct to be used in an underlier.
members.name: cdm/product/template/Product

members.description: A data type to specify the financial product's economic terms, alongside the product identification and product taxonomy. The non-transferable product data type represents a product that can be traded (as part of a TradableProduct) but cannot be transferred to others.  It is meant to be used across the pre-execution, execution and (as part of the Contract) post-execution lifecycle contexts.

economicTerms.description: The price forming features, including payouts and provisions.

identifier.description: Comprises a identifier and a source to uniquely identify the nonTransferableProduct.

members.name: cdm/product/template/NonTransferableProduct

taxonomy.description: Specifies the product taxonomy, which is composed of a taxonomy value and a taxonomy source.

delivery.description: Contains the information relative to the delivery of the asset.

members.description: The option payout specification terms. The associated globalKey denotes the ability to associate a hash value to the respective OptionPayout instantiation for the purpose of model cross-referencing, in support of functionality such as the event effect and the lineage.

exerciseTerms.description: The terms for exercising the option, which include the option style (e.g. American style option), the exercise procedure (e.g. manual exercise) and the settlement terms (e.g. physical vs. cash).

feature.description: The option feature, such as quanto, Asian, barrier, knock.

members.name: cdm/product/template/OptionPayout

observationTerms.description: Class containing terms that are associated with observing a price/benchmark/index across either single or multple observations. To be used for option contracts that reference a benchmark price.

optionType.description: The type of option transaction. From a usage standpoint, put/call is the default option type, while payer/receiver indicator is used for options on index credit default swaps, consistently with the industry practice. Straddle is used for the case of straddle strategy, that combine a call and a put with the same strike.

payerReceiver.description: Canonical representation of the payer and receiver parties applicable to each payout leg.

priceQuantity.description: Each payout leg must implement the quantity concept as a 'resolvable' type, which allows for different payout legs to be linked to each other (e.g. in the case of cross-curreny products).

principalPayment.description: The specification of the principal exchange. Optional as only applicable in the case of cross-currency or zero-coupon swaps with a final payment.

schedule.description: Allows the full representation of a payout by defining a set of schedule periods. It supports standard schedule customization by expressing all the dates, quantities, and pricing data in a non-parametric way.

settlementTerms.description: Each payout leg must specifies its settlement terms, including the delivery type (i.e. cash vs physical, and their respective terms), the transfer type (DvP etc.) and settlement date, if any.

strike.description: Specifies the strike of the option

underlier.description: The financial product underlying the option, which can be of any type including an Asset, Basket, Index or a NonTransferableProduct.

Observable.description: Specifies the object to be observed for a price, it could be an asset or a reference.

Product.description: Enables either a TransferableProduct or a NonTransferableProduct to be used in an underlier.

members.description: The underlying financial product that will be physically or cash settled, which can be of any type, eg an asset such as cash or a security, a product, or the cash settlement of an index rate.  Conditions are usually applied when used in a data type, such as a payout, to ensure this aligns with the use case.
members.name: cdm/product/template/Underlier

members.description: Contains the necessary specifications for all performance payouts, encompassing equity return, dividend, variance, volatility and correlation products.

finalValuationPrice.description: Specifies the net final valuation price(s) of the underlier at Performance Payout level. This price can be expressed either as an actual amount/currency, as a determination method, or by reference to another value specified in the swap document.

fxFeature.description: Defines quanto or composite FX features that are included in the swap leg.

initialValuationPrice.description: Specifies the net initial valuation price(s) of the underlier at Performance Payout level. This price can be expressed either as an actual amount/currency, as a determination method, or by reference to another value specified in the swap document.

interimValuationPrice.description: Specifies the net initial valuation price(s) of the underlier at Performance Payout level. This price can be expressed either as an actual amount/currency, as a determination method, or by reference to another value specified in the swap document.

members.name: cdm/product/template/PerformancePayout

observationTerms.description: Defines how and when a performance type option or performance type swap is to be observed.

payerReceiver.description: Canonical representation of the payer and receiver parties applicable to each payout leg.

paymentDates.description: Defines the payment date schedule, as defined by the parameters that are needed to specify it, either in a parametric way or by reference to another schedule of dates (e.g. the valuation dates).

portfolioReturnTerms.description: Specifies an individual type of return of a Performance Payout, when such individual return is part of an aggregation of multiple similar returns, at Performance Payout level

priceQuantity.description: Each payout leg must implement the quantity concept as a 'resolvable' type, which allows for different payout legs to be linked to each other (e.g. in the case of cross-curreny products).

principalPayment.description: The specification of the principal exchange. Optional as only applicable in the case of cross-currency or zero-coupon swaps with a final payment.

returnTerms.description: Specifies the type of return of a performance payout.

settlementTerms.description: Each payout leg must specifies its settlement terms, including the delivery type (i.e. cash vs physical, and their respective terms), the transfer type (DvP etc.) and settlement date, if any.

underlier.description: Identifies the underlying product that is referenced for pricing of the applicable leg in a swap.  Referenced in the '2018 ISDA CDM Equity Confirmation for Security Equity Swap' as Security.

valuationDates.description: Defines how and when a performance type option or performance type swap is to be valued, including both interim and final valuation.

Cash.description: An Asset that consists solely of a monetary holding in a currency.

Commodity.description: An Asset comprised of raw or refined materials or agricultural products, eg gold, oil or wheat.

DigitalAsset.description: An Asset that exists only in digital form, eg Bitcoin or Ethereum; excludes the digital representation of other Assets.

Instrument.description: An asset that is issued by one party to one or more others; Instrument is also a choice data type.

members.description: A TransferableProduct is a type of financial product which can be held or transferred, represented as an Asset with the addition of specific EconomicTerms.

economicTerms.description: The price forming features, including payouts and provisions.

members.name: cdm/product/template/TransferableProduct

delivery.description: Contains the information relative to the delivery of the asset.

deliveryTerm.description: Also called contract month or delivery month. However, it's not always a month. It is usually expressed using a code, e.g. Z23 would be the Dec 2023 contract, (Z = December). For crude oil, the corresponding contract might be called CLZ23.

members.description: Represents a forward settling payout. The underlier attribute captures the underlying payout, which is settled according to the settlementTerms attribute (which is part of PayoutBase). Both FX Spot and FX Forward should use this component.
members.name: cdm/product/template/SettlementPayout

payerReceiver.description: Canonical representation of the payer and receiver parties applicable to each payout leg.

priceQuantity.description: Each payout leg must implement the quantity concept as a 'resolvable' type, which allows for different payout legs to be linked to each other (e.g. in the case of cross-curreny products).

principalPayment.description: The specification of the principal exchange. Optional as only applicable in the case of cross-currency or zero-coupon swaps with a final payment.

schedule.description: Allows the full representation of a payout by defining a set of schedule periods. It supports standard schedule customization by expressing all the dates, quantities, and pricing data in a non-parametric way.

settlementTerms.description: Each payout leg must specifies its settlement terms, including the delivery type (i.e. cash vs physical, and their respective terms), the transfer type (DvP etc.) and settlement date, if any.

underlier.description: The underlying financial product that will be physically or cash settled, which can be of any type, eg an asset such as cash or a security, or the cash settlement of an index rate.

averagingFeature.description: Indicates if the averaging calculation, when applicable, is weighted or unweighted.

calculationPeriodDates.description: Defines the calculation period dates schedule.

commodityPriceReturnTerms.description: Defines parameters in which the commodity price is assessed.

delivery.description: Contains the information relative to the delivery of the asset.

members.description: Payout based on the averaged price of a referenced underlier. (e.g. Commodities). Can represent both average (average of many) & bullet (average of 1) pricing

fxFeature.description: Defines quanto or composite FX features that are included in the swap leg.

members.name: cdm/product/asset/CommodityPayout

payerReceiver.description: Canonical representation of the payer and receiver parties applicable to each payout leg.

paymentDates.description: Defines the payment date schedule, as defined by the parameters that are needed to specify it, either in a parametric way or by reference to another schedule of dates (e.g. the valuation dates).

priceQuantity.description: Each payout leg must implement the quantity concept as a 'resolvable' type, which allows for different payout legs to be linked to each other (e.g. in the case of cross-curreny products).

pricingDates.description: Specifies specific dates or parametric rules for the dates on which the price will be determined.

principalPayment.description: The specification of the principal exchange. Optional as only applicable in the case of cross-currency or zero-coupon swaps with a final payment.

schedule.description: Allows the full representation of a payout by defining a set of schedule periods. It supports standard schedule customization by expressing all the dates, quantities, and pricing data in a non-parametric way.

settlementTerms.description: Each payout leg must specifies its settlement terms, including the delivery type (i.e. cash vs physical, and their respective terms), the transfer type (DvP etc.) and settlement date, if any.

underlier.description: Identifies the underlying product that is referenced for pricing of the applicable leg in a swap. Referenced in the '2018 ISDA CDM Equity Confirmation for Security Equity Swap' as Security.

calculationAgent.description: The ISDA calculation agent responsible for performing duties as defined in the applicable product definitions.

collateral.description: Represents the collateral obligations of a party.

dateAdjustments.description: The business day adjustment convention when it applies across all the payout components. This specification of the business day convention and financial business centers is used for adjusting any calculation period date if it would otherwise fall on a day that is not a business day in the specified business center.

members.description: This class represents the full set of price-forming features associated with a contractual product: the payout component, the notional/quantity, the effective and termination date and the date adjustment provisions when applying uniformily across the payout components. This class also includes the legal provisions which have valuation implications: cancelable provision, extendible provision, early termination provision and extraordinary events specification.

effectiveDate.description: The first day of the terms of the trade. This day may be subject to adjustment in accordance with a business day convention.

members.name: cdm/product/template/EconomicTerms

nonStandardisedTerms.description: Specifies, when boolean value is True, that additional economic terms exist that have not been included in the product representation.

payout.description: The payout specifies the future cashflow computation methodology which characterizes a financial product.

terminationDate.description: The last day of the terms of the trade. This date may be subject to adjustments in accordance with the business day convention. It can also be specified in relation to another scheduled date (e.g. the last payment date).

terminationProvision.description: Contains optional provisions pertaining to the termination characteristics of a contract.

AssetPayout.description: Defines the assets and movements in a security financing transaction.

CommodityPayout.description: Defines the payout for the floating leg of a Commodity Swap.

CreditDefaultPayout.description: The credit default payout, which provides the details necessary for determining when a credit payout will be triggered as well as the parameters for calculating the payout and the settlement terms.

FixedPricePayout.description: Defines a payout in which one or more payouts are defined as a fixed price.

InterestRatePayout.description: All of the terms necessary to define and calculate a cash flow based on a fixed, a floating or an inflation index rate. The interest rate payout can be applied to interest rate swaps and FRA (which both have two associated interest rate payouts), credit default swaps (to represent the fee leg when subject to periodic payments) and equity swaps (to represent the funding leg).

PerformancePayout.description: The performance payout, which encompasses the equity price returns, dividend returns, volatility return, variance return and correlation provisions.

SettlementPayout.description: Represents a forward settling payout. The 'Underlier' attribute captures the underlying payout, which is settled according to the 'SettlementTerms' attribute. Both FX Spot and FX Forward should use this component.

members.description: Represents the set of future cashflow methodologies in the form of specific payout data type(s) which result from the financial product.  Examples: a trade in a cash asset will use only a settlement payout; for derivatives, two interest rate payouts can be combined to specify an interest rate swap; one interest rate payout can be combined with a credit default payout to specify a credit default swap.

CommodityPayout.description: Defines the payout for the floating leg of a Commodity Swap.

CreditDefaultPayout.description: The credit default payout, which provides the details necessary for determining when a credit payout will be triggered as well as the parameters for calculating the payout and the settlement terms.

FixedPricePayout.description: Defines a payout in which one or more payouts are defined as a fixed price.

InterestRatePayout.description: All of the terms necessary to define and calculate a cash flow based on a fixed, a floating or an inflation index rate. The interest rate payout can be applied to interest rate swaps and FRA (which both have two associated interest rate payouts), credit default swaps (to represent the fee leg when subject to periodic payments) and equity swaps (to represent the funding leg).

PerformancePayout.description: The performance payout, which encompasses the equity price returns, dividend returns, volatility return, variance return and correlation provisions.

SettlementPayout.description: Represents a forward settling payout. The 'Underlier' attribute captures the underlying payout, which is settled according to the 'SettlementTerms' attribute. Both FX Spot and FX Forward should use this component.

members.description: Represents the set of future cashflow methodologies in the form of specific payout data type(s) which result from the financial product. principalPayment.description: The specification of the principal exchange. Optional as only applicable in the case of cross-currency or zero-coupon swaps with a final payment.

schedule.description: Allows the full representation of a payout by defining a set of schedule periods. It supports standard schedule customization by expressing all the dates, quantities, and pricing data in a non-parametric way.

settlementTerms.description: Each payout leg must specifies its settlement terms, including the delivery type (i.e. cash vs physical, and their respective terms), the transfer type (DvP etc.) and settlement date, if any.

underlier.description: The underlying financial product that will be physically or cash settled, which can be of any type, eg an asset such as cash or a security, or the cash settlement of an index rate.

NonTransferableProduct.description: The non-transferable product data type represents a product that can be traded (as part of a TradableProduct) but cannot be transferred to others.

TransferableProduct.description: A TransferableProduct is a type of financial product which can be held or transferred, represented as an Asset with the addition of specific EconomicTerms.

members.description: Enables either a TransferableProduct or a NonTransferableProduct to be used in an underlier.

identifier.description: Comprises a identifier and a source to uniquely identify the nonTransferableProduct.

taxonomy.description: Specifies the product taxonomy, which is composed of a taxonomy value and a taxonomy source.

delivery.description: Contains the information relative to the delivery of the asset.

members.description: The option payout specification terms. The associated globalKey denotes the ability to associate a hash value to the respective OptionPayout instantiation for the purpose of model cross-referencing, in support of functionality such as the event effect and the lineage.

exerciseTerms.description: The terms for exercising the option, which include the option style (e.g. American style option), the exercise procedure (e.g. manual exercise) and the settlement terms (e.g. physical vs. cash).

feature.description: The option feature, such as quanto, Asian, barrier, knock.

settlementTerms.description: Each payout leg must specifies its settlement terms, including the delivery type (i.e. cash vs physical, and their respective terms), the transfer type (DvP etc.) and settlement date, if any.

collateral.description: Represents the collateral obligations of a party.

nonStandardisedTerms.description: Specifies, when boolean value is True, that additional economic terms exist that have not been included in the product representation.

payout.description: The payout specifies the future cashflow computation methodology which characterizes a financial product.

terminationDate.description: The last day of the terms of the trade. This date may be subject to adjustments in accordance with the business day convention. It can also be specified in relation to another scheduled date (e.g. the last payment date).

terminationProvision.description: Contains optional provisions pertaining to the termination characteristics of a contract.

AssetPayout.description: Defines the assets and movements in a security financing transaction.

CommodityPayout.description: Defines the payout for the floating leg of a Commodity Swap.

CreditDefaultPayout.description: The credit default payout, which provides the details necessary for determining when a credit payout will be triggered as well as the parameters for calculating the payout and the settlement terms.

FixedPricePayout.description: Defines a payout in which one or more payouts are defined as a fixed price.

InterestRatePayout.description: All of the terms necessary to define and calculate a cash flow based on a fixed, a floating or an inflation index rate. The interest rate payout can be applied to interest rate swaps and FRA (which both have two associated interest rate payouts), credit default swaps (to represent the fee leg when subject to periodic payments) and equity swaps (to represent the funding leg).

PerformancePayout.description: The performance payout, which encompasses the equity price returns, dividend returns, volatility return, variance return and correlation provisions.

SettlementPayout.description: Represents a forward settling payout. The 'Underlier' attribute captures the underlying payout, which is settled according to the 'SettlementTerms' attribute. Both FX Spot and FX Forward should use this component.

members.description: Represents the set of future cashflow methodologies in the form of specific payout data type(s) which result from the financial product.  Examples: a trade in a cash asset will use only a settlement payout; for derivatives, two interest rate payouts can be combined to specify an interest rate swap; one interest rate payout can be combined with a credit default payout to specify a credit default swap.

FixedPricePayout.description: Defines a payout in which one or more payouts are defined as a fixed price.

InterestRatePayout.description: All of the terms necessary to define and calculate a cash flow based on a fixed, a floating or an inflation index rate. members.description: Represents the set of future cashflow methodologies in the form of specific payout data type(s) which result from the financial product.  Examples: a trade in a cash asset will use only a settlement payout; for derivatives, two interest rate payouts can be combined to specify an interest rate swap; one interest rate payout can be combined with a credit default payout to specify a credit default swap.

The actor bound to agreementProposerChannel offers the exact Agreement. The
actor bound to agreementAcceptorChannel may accept it. Either participant may
invoke the standard suspension, resumption, completion, or termination
operations through agreementControlChannel. Concrete Agreement profiles may
narrow those rights by replacing the Channel bindings or by defining
additional Operations that emit the standard lifecycle Messages.

The base type owns deterministic initialization, acceptance, activation,
suspension, resumption, completion, termination, lifecycle timestamps,
lifecycle Messages, and graceful processing termination. It also declares
/orders as a Process Embedded collection. A concrete profile may add other
managed documents and event-driven policies without replacing these inherited
lifecycle transitions.

Participants are the exact Timeline Channels under /contracts. Agreement
clauses are direct workflow contracts, not ordinary list values. Document
Section markers connect ordinary Agreement content and state to the contracts
that interpret or mutate it.

{"apiKeyId":{"description":"Opaque or provider-defined identifier of the API credential, client registration, integration, or signing key used to
submit the request. It should be stable enough for the provider and authorized auditors to trace, revoke, and review
the credential, but it need not reveal secret credential material.
","type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"}},"description":"Source specialization for a programmatic request submitted through an API credential, service integration, client
registration, signed request, webhook, or similar non-interactive interface. API Call identifies the submission
channel; it does not by itself say whether the actor was a principal, an agent, or another provider-defined actor.

API Call is useful because many documents distinguish low-risk automation from high-risk principal actions. A bank
transfer document might allow API calls to add notes or upload receipts, while requiring an interactive browser
session for final authorization. A procurement workflow might allow an agent to request quotes through an API but not
to commit funds. These decisions belong to Blue documents and processor policies, not to the Timeline Provider.

The provider's responsibility is to authenticate the API credential or client under its infrastructure rules,
confirm that the caller is allowed to append to the relevant timeline or submit the relevant event, and record the
source attribution accurately. The provider does not need to know what every Blue document will later do with the
message.
","name":"API Call","type":{"blueId":"Qm35f9xFUH84i745uPMj5jjMX1oCCG79aeSfHViipxG"}}

{"channels":{"description":"Same-scope contract-map keys of Timeline Channel contracts included in this composite. The list order is not a
cross-timeline ordering rule; event ordering must be established by the feeder/provider layer and deterministic
processor sorting.
","itemType":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"type":{"blueId":"85ip88snCGrgUNdi1rUFqqAxcxwVGKV2g4LjsKoyKmXK"}},"description":"Channel contract that groups several same-scope Timeline Channels into one union channel. A Composite Timeline
Channel matches when any referenced child channel would accept the delivered event. It is useful when a workflow
should react to a family of participant timelines while binding handlers to one logical channel key.

The composite has no timeline or actor of its own. Each referenced Timeline Channel supplies its own timeline and actor
binding, and the composite delegates event eligibility to those children. If several children accept the same entry,
the composite produces one logical delivery to handlers bound to the composite key. The composite's checkpoint is
independent from checkpoints of child channels used directly elsewhere in the document.

This type does not create global consensus and does not collapse the child timelines into one storage log. Each child
timeline retains its provider, completeness, actor attribution, and trust model. The composite only simplifies routing
inside the document. A correct feeder/processor must still preserve deterministic ordering across the relevant
timelines using provider completeness guarantees and the Blue Contracts checkpoint model.
","name":"Composite Timeline Channel","type":{"blueId":"CaFMD5Tpz4LbGjJsftT3465hKBWa7Ti6dutYHnCSRQyR"}}

{"bankruptcy":{"description":"A credit event. The reference entity has been dissolved or has become insolvent. It also covers events that may be a precursor to insolvency such as instigation of bankruptcy or insolvency proceedings. Sovereign trades are not subject to Bankruptcy as 'technically' a Sovereign cannot become bankrupt. ISDA 2003 Term: Bankruptcy.
","type":{"blueId":"AwvXD961fmnmqcSQhjMA7r15HpVh39cefb6ZTyUz2Fm2"}},"creditEventNotice":{"description":"A specified condition to settlement. An irrevocable written or verbal notice that describes a credit event that has occurred. The notice is sent from the notifying party (either the buyer or the seller) to the counterparty. It provides information relevant to determining that a credit event has occurred. This is typically accompanied by Publicly Available Information. ISDA 2003 Term: Credit Event Notice.
","type":{"blueId":"7y5f3qP5VjXYPT8a7V7Fxtq2Zk1KpeGGDfWTMhRHhyaB"}},"defaultRequirement":{"description":"In relation to certain credit events, serves as a threshold for Obligation Acceleration, Obligation Default, Repudiation/Moratorium and Restructuring. Market standard is USD 10,000,000 (JPY 1,000,000,000 for all Japanese Yen trades). This is applied on an aggregate or total basis across all Obligations of the Reference Entity. Used to prevent technical/operational errors from triggering credit events. ISDA 2003 Term: Default Requirement.
","type":{"blueId":"8eHxH2MmvpRLFkatvGU4hggBkuvX59UqJSYpXnjwG5hL"}},"description":"A class to specify the applicable Credit Events that would trigger a settlement, as specified in the related Confirmation and defined in the ISDA 2014 Credit Definition article IV section 4.1.
","distressedRatingsDowngrade":{"description":"A credit event. Results from the fact that the rating of the reference obligation is down-graded to a distressed rating level. From a usage standpoint, this credit event is typically not applicable in case of RMBS trades.
","type":{"blueId":"AwvXD961fmnmqcSQhjMA7r15HpVh39cefb6ZTyUz2Fm2"}},"failureToPay":{"description":"A credit event. This credit event triggers, after the expiration of any applicable grace period, if the reference entity fails to make due payments in an aggregate amount of not less than the payment requirement on one or more obligations (e.g. a missed coupon payment). ISDA 2003 Term: Failure to Pay.
","type":{"blueId":"3HK4oc4hgEvobnEKfiz71KcskdHXwhrFwQPbCSCzgsAW"}},"failureToPayInterest":{"description":"A credit event. Corresponds to the failure by the Reference Entity to pay an expected interest amount or the payment of an actual interest amount that is less than the expected interest amount. ISDA 2003 Term: Failure to Pay Interest.
","type":{"blueId":"AwvXD961fmnmqcSQhjMA7r15HpVh39cefb6ZTyUz2Fm2"}},"failureToPayPrincipal":{"description":"A credit event. Corresponds to the failure by the Reference Entity to pay an expected principal amount or the payment of an actual principal amount that is less than the expected principal amount. ISDA 2003 Term: Failure to Pay Principal.
","type":{"blueId":"AwvXD961fmnmqcSQhjMA7r15HpVh39cefb6ZTyUz2Fm2"}},"governmentalIntervention":{"description":"A credit event. A governmental intervention is an event resulting from an action by a governmental authority that materially impacts the reference entity's obligations, such as an interest rate reduction, principal reduction, deferral of interest or principal, change in priority ranking, or change in currency or composition of payment. ISDA 2014 Term: Governmental Intervention.
","type":{"blueId":"AwvXD961fmnmqcSQhjMA7r15HpVh39cefb6ZTyUz2Fm2"}},"impliedWritedown":{"description":"A credit event. Results from the fact that losses occur to the underlying instruments that do not result in reductions of the outstanding principal of the reference obligation.
","type":{"blueId":"AwvXD961fmnmqcSQhjMA7r15HpVh39cefb6ZTyUz2Fm2"}},"maturityExtension":{"description":"A credit event. Results from the fact that the underlier fails to make principal payments as expected.","type":{"blueId":"AwvXD961fmnmqcSQhjMA7r15HpVh39cefb6ZTyUz2Fm2"}},"name":"cdm/observable/event/CreditEvents","obligationAcceleration":{"description":"A credit event. One or more of the obligations have been declared due and payable before they would otherwise have been due and payable as a result of, or on the basis of, the occurrence of a default, event of default or other similar condition or event other than failure to pay (preferred by the market over Obligation Default, because more definitive and encompasses the definition of Obligation Default - this is more favorable to the Seller). Subject to the default requirement amount. ISDA 2003 Term: Obligation Acceleration.
","type":{"blueId":"AwvXD961fmnmqcSQhjMA7r15HpVh39cefb6ZTyUz2Fm2"}},"obligationDefault":{"description":"A credit event. One or more of the obligations have become capable of being declared due and payable before they would otherwise have been due and payable as a result of, or on the basis of, the occurrence of a default, event of default or other similar condition or event other than failure to pay. ISDA 2003 Term: Obligation Default.
","type":{"blueId":"AwvXD961fmnmqcSQhjMA7r15HpVh39cefb6ZTyUz2Fm2"}},"repudiationMoratorium":{"description":"A credit event. The reference entity, or a governmental authority, either refuses to recognise or challenges the validity of one or more obligations of the reference entity, or imposes a moratorium thereby postponing payments on one or more of the obligations of the reference entity. Subject to the default requirement amount. ISDA 2003 Term: Repudiation/Moratorium.
","type":{"blueId":"AwvXD961fmnmqcSQhjMA7r15HpVh39cefb6ZTyUz2Fm2"}},"restructuring":{"description":"A credit event. A restructuring is an event that materially impacts the reference entity's obligations, such as an interest rate reduction, principal reduction, deferral of interest or principal, change in priority ranking, or change in currency or composition of payment. ISDA 2003 Term: Restructuring.
","type":{"blueId":"8pTRZ8d4Ri1ECATE8XxQBSaJij5kGuLtCzx3iJjDHJ8K"}},"writedown":{"description":"A credit event. Results from the fact that the underlier writes down its outstanding principal amount.","type":{"blueId":"AwvXD961fmnmqcSQhjMA7r15HpVh39cefb6ZTyUz2Fm2"}}}

payload as a normal coordination event so it appears in document event projections and audit views.

Sequential Workflow Operation defines steps as append-only. Chat Workflow Operation seeds that list with a standard
first step that emits the chat event that arrived in the operation request; document-specific chat behavior can append
validation, moderation, indexing, notification, or projection steps after that standard emission step without changing
the inherited prefix.

domain-specific operations and strong response types for machine-actionable commitments.

{"description":"Specifies the parameters to generate the payment date schedule, either through a parametric representation or by reference to specified dates.
","firstPaymentDate":{"description":"The first unadjusted payment date. This day may be subject to adjustment in accordance with any business day convention specified in paymentDatesAdjustments. This element must only be included if there is an initial stub. This date will normally correspond to an unadjusted calculation period start or end date. This is true even if early or delayed payment is specified to be applicable since the actual first payment date will be the specified number of days before or after the applicable adjusted calculation period start or end date with the resulting payment date then being adjusted in accordance with any business day convention specified in paymentDatesAdjustments.
","type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"}},"lastRegularPaymentDate":{"description":"The last regular payment date when specified as a date, as in the FpML interest rate construct. FpML specifies that this date may be subject to adjustment in accordance with any business day convention specified in the paymentDatesAdjustments attribute.
","type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"}},"name":"cdm/product/common/schedule/PaymentDates","payRelativeTo":{"description":"Specifies whether the payments occur relative to each adjusted calculation period start date or end date, each reset date, valuation date or the last pricing date. Calculation period start date means relative to the start of the first calculation period contributing to a given payment. Similarly, calculation period end date means the end of the last calculation period contributing to a given payment. The valuation date is applicable for Brazilian-CDI and equity swaps.
","type":{"blueId":"4EzoEo3dUznVuJ5u3FRBicnYoijDtwyRj3XLQxEdE1Hn"}},"paymentDateSchedule":{"description":"The payment dates when specified as relative to a set of dates specified somewhere else in the instance document/transaction, e.g. the valuation dates as typically the case for equity swaps, or when specified as a calculation period schedule.
","type":{"blueId":"H2x8AcpWBE1vPg4EgJ99gzTwGrWbNkrkhsgom7gvbRLB"}},"paymentDatesAdjustments":{"description":"The definition of the business day convention and financial business centers used for adjusting the payment date if it would otherwise fall on a day that is not a business day in the specified business center.
","type":{"blueId":"HZJDnv878jZDzx4XhQtskoT3SAT9j2YgYkiuAfxKPXsS"}},"paymentDaysOffset":{"description":"If early payment or delayed payment is required, specifies the number of days offset that the payment occurs relative to what would otherwise be the unadjusted payment date. The offset can be specified in terms of either calendar or business days. Even in the case of a calendar days offset, the resulting payment date, adjusted for the specified calendar days offset, will still be adjusted in accordance with the specified payment dates adjustments. This element should only be included if early or delayed payment is applicable, i.e. if the periodMultiplier element value is not equal to zero. An early payment would be indicated by a negative periodMultiplier element value and a delayed payment (or payment lag) would be indicated by a positive periodMultiplier element value.
","type":{"blueId":"GWTMGPw1zgQW3M9NUS6RxNtce5jWU9defVNkm7sV6b8L"}},"paymentFrequency":{"description":"The frequency at which regular payment dates occur. If the payment frequency is equal to the frequency defined in the calculation period dates component then one calculation period contributes to each payment amount. If the payment frequency is less frequent than the frequency defined in the calculation period dates component then more than one calculation period will contribute to the payment amount. A payment frequency more frequent than the calculation period frequency or one that is not a multiple of the calculation period frequency is invalid. If the payment frequency is of value T (term), the period is defined by the effectiveDate and the terminationDate.
","type":{"blueId":"2DcHFUdmvnUmoKpU2Ams5asKp2FjTWgEDMMrEiZUL3Bi"}}}

{"description":"A class to provide lineage information across lifecycle events through a pointer or set of pointers into the event(s), contract(s) and, possibly, payout components that the event is dependent on or relates to. As an example, if an contractFormation event is corrected, the correction event will have a lineage into the initial event, which takes the form of a globalKey into that initial contract formation event. Two referencing mechanisms are provided as part of the CDM: either the globalKey, which corresponds to the hash value of the CDM class which is referred to, or a reference qualifier which is meant to provide support for the ingestion of xml documents with id/href mechanisms. The CDM recommends the use of the globalKey and provides a default implementation which is accessible in the generated code through org.isda.cdm.globalKey.GlobalKeyHashCalculator. If implementers want to use an alternative hashing mechanism, the API in which they need to plug it is com.rosetta.model.lib.HashFunction.
","eventReference":{"description":"The reference to the instantiation of an Event object, either through a globalKey or an xml-derived id/href mechanism. {"description":"Mandate authorizing the actor bound to authorizedActorChannel to invoke one
named operation through one exact effective channel, on behalf of the actor
bound to authorityHolderChannel.

It may be used on any target where the authority-holder actor participates in
the declared effective channel and all inherited lifecycle, actor, channel,
operation, document-version, and optional validation checks pass.

The inherited validation field examines the nested Operation Request.request
payload through its immutable request binding. It does not examine the target
document or Operation Request envelope.

Optional target.documentValidation examines only the frozen resolved target
root immediately before the candidate Timeline Entry. Its absence imposes no
target-document identity, type, or content restriction.
","name":"Operation Mandate","target":{"channel":{"description":"Exact effective target channel authorized by this mandate.","schema":{"required":{"type":{"blueId":"AwvXD961fmnmqcSQhjMA7r15HpVh39cefb6ZTyUz2Fm2"},"value":true}},"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"}},"documentValidation":{"description":"Optional deterministic target-document validation. Absence imposes no
document identity, type, or content restriction. When present, at least
one matcher is required and both configured matchers must pass.
","document":{"description":"Optional structural Blue pattern matched candidate-first against the
frozen resolved target root immediately before the candidate entry.
Extra fields in the candidate are allowed; every omitted field is
unconstrained.
"},"function":{"description":"Optional deterministic BEX validation program represented as a Blue
node. The host exposes $document as the exact resolved Mandate root and
targetDocument as the sole immutable candidate binding containing the
frozen resolved pre-entry target root.

It does not expose the operation request or other ambient bindings.
Request validation belongs to the inherited validation field.

Only Boolean true passes. False, null, undefined, a non-Boolean result,
compilation failure, execution failure, or resource-limit failure
rejects the candidate.
"}},"operation":{"description":"Single target operation authorized by this mandate.","schema":{"required":{"type":{"blueId":"AwvXD961fmnmqcSQhjMA7r15HpVh39cefb6ZTyUz2Fm2"},"value":true}},"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"}},"schema":{"required":{"type":{"blueId":"AwvXD961fmnmqcSQhjMA7r15HpVh39cefb6ZTyUz2Fm2"},"value":true}}},"type":{"blueId":"BByueMvVs5WhBfNQQ54iHtXPeFcpNXDs4tJVFKaL86pW"}}

No implicit stubs are allowed, i.e. stubs must be explicitly specified using an appropriate combination of firstPeriodStartDate, firstRegularPeriodStartDate and lastRegularPeriodEndDate.
","effectiveDate":{"description":"The first day of the terms of the trade. This day may be subject to adjustment in accordance with a business day convention.

","type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"}},"firstPeriodStartDate":{"description":"The start date of the calculation period. ","type":{"blueId":"9bWLoL1zcJYR9saaAKGg2PbRC5k5kMqn4CktUzBBfgeY"}},"firstRegularPeriodStartDate":{"description":"The start date of the regular part of the calculation period schedule. ","type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"}},"lastRegularPeriodEndDate":{"description":"The end date of the regular part of the calculation period schedule. {"activateOnAuthorityConfirmation":{"description":"Controls whether successful authority confirmation also emits the mandate
activation Message.

When true, successful confirmation emits Mandate/Mandate Activated, which
is handled by the inherited activation workflow.

When false, successful confirmation leaves the mandate in
Mandate/Status Authority Confirmed. A specialized operation must later emit
Mandate/Mandate Activated.

When absent before initialization, the initialization workflow materializes
true. The field is not a fixed inherited value, so a concrete mandate may
explicitly set it to false.
","type":{"blueId":"AwvXD961fmnmqcSQhjMA7r15HpVh39cefb6ZTyUz2Fm2"}},"activatedAt":{"description":"Microsecond timestamp from which the mandate entered Mandate/Status Active.

The value is derived by the inherited activation workflow from the root
causal Coordination/Timeline Entry that led to the accepted
Mandate/Mandate Activated Message. It is not supplied by that Message.
After activation succeeds, inherited lifecycle workflows do not replace
it.
","type":{"blueId":"E2LM6qgzWG9ttagq2xTmiZkgYEAgkYedFCmU9v7NnVEq"}},"authorityConfirmedAt":{"description":"Microsecond timestamp of the root causal Coordination/Timeline Entry that
successfully changed the mandate from Coordination/Status Pending to
Mandate/Status Authority Confirmed.

The value is derived by the inherited authority-confirmation workflow. It
is never supplied by the operation request. After authority confirmation
succeeds, inherited lifecycle workflows do not replace it.
","type":{"blueId":"E2LM6qgzWG9ttagq2xTmiZkgYEAgkYedFCmU9v7NnVEq"}},"contracts":{"applyMandateActivation":{"channel":{"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"mandateActivatedChannel"},"description":"Sole authoritative mandate-activation implementation.

It accepts Mandate/Mandate Activated emitted by an operation. On
Mandate/Status Authority Confirmed it changes status to Mandate/Status
Active and records activatedAt from the root causal Timeline Entry. The
Message itself does not supply the timestamp and is not emitted again.

On Coordination/Status Pending, Mandate/Status Active,
Mandate/Status Terminated, or Coordination/Status Failed it performs no
lifecycle mutation and does not replace activatedAt.

A Message without a root causal Timeline Entry cannot establish an
activation timestamp and must not activate the mandate.

Concrete workflow steps and BEX implementation are defined in this base
type.
","event":{"type":{"blueId":"3HtuEaYgkn8rV9xZf1x5uY2v7S9WXbVkcV3rj3Sy6arJ"}},"steps":[{"definition":{"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"mandateLifecycleDefinition"},"entry":{"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"applyMandateActivation"},"name":"Apply Mandate Activation","type":{"blueId":"HLwXH1Zsw9LBcFeueCCo776WxauAU8SWsHGcaarNdTab"}}],"type":{"blueId":"4twSW1MCdf7UMzfwcu99gcBDZiiND1tSC2YZoFMVNHPf"}},"applyMandateTermination":{"channel":{"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"mandateTerminatedChannel"},"description":"Sole authoritative mandate-termination implementation.

It accepts Mandate/Mandate Terminated emitted by an operation. On
Coordination/Status Pending, Mandate/Status Authority Confirmed, or
Mandate/Status Active it changes status to Mandate/Status Terminated and
records terminatedAt from the root causal Timeline Entry. The Message
itself carries the required reason and correlation, does not supply the
timestamp, and is not emitted again. Its reason is propagated unchanged
to the graceful processor termination request.

The Compute result requests graceful termination after its state changes
and emitted events have been buffered. Coordination validates the complete
result before applying effects, then applies changes, emits events, and
requests graceful termination in that order.

On Mandate/Status Terminated or Coordination/Status Failed it performs no
lifecycle mutation and does not replace terminatedAt. Receipt of the
termination Message still requests graceful processing termination, so a
failed mandate can be stopped without replacing its failure state.

Concrete workflow steps and BEX implementation are defined in this base
type. No dedicated termination workflow-step type is required.
","event":{"type":{"blueId":"C3Y1zAyhCiu9wJ23gYg6vqFnVQyXKZeiHow9CzJ4W9t7"}},"steps":[{"definition":{"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"mandateLifecycleDefinition"},"entry":{"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"applyMandateTermination"},"name":"Apply Mandate Termination","type":{"blueId":"HLwXH1Zsw9LBcFeueCCo776WxauAU8SWsHGcaarNdTab"}}],"type":{"blueId":"4twSW1MCdf7UMzfwcu99gcBDZiiND1tSC2YZoFMVNHPf"}},"authorityHolderChannel":{"description":"Required participant channel whose actor controls the authority or
resource delegated by this mandate. The authority holder may invoke the
standard termination operation.
","schema":{"required":{"type":{"blueId":"AwvXD961fmnmqcSQhjMA7r15HpVh39cefb6ZTyUz2Fm2"},"value":true}},"type":{"blueId":"8aohWT7jcoaC1j2siQzBxoKM8HhQ4HF13BkZDNnq5UHf"}},"authorizedActorChannel":{"description":"Required participant channel whose actor receives the delegated
authority. Concrete mandate subtypes define the delegated resource,
action, target, or request semantics.
","schema":{"required":{"type":{"blueId":"AwvXD961fmnmqcSQhjMA7r15HpVh39cefb6ZTyUz2Fm2"},"value":true}},"type":{"blueId":"8aohWT7jcoaC1j2siQzBxoKM8HhQ4HF13BkZDNnq5UHf"}},"confirmMandateAuthority":{"channel":{"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"mandateGuarantorChannel"},"description":"Inherited operation through which the guarantor confirms that the
declared authority relationship is legitimate.

On Coordination/Status Pending it changes status to
Mandate/Status Authority Confirmed, records authorityConfirmedAt
from the root causal Timeline Entry, emits Mandate/Mandate Authority
Confirmed, and, when activateOnAuthorityConfirmation is not false, emits
Mandate/Mandate Activated for the inherited activation workflow.

On Mandate/Status Authority Confirmed, Mandate/Status Active,
Mandate/Status Terminated, or Coordination/Status Failed it performs no
lifecycle mutation and does not replace authorityConfirmedAt.

A guarantor may choose to use Operation Request.document and
requireExactDocumentVersion to pin the reviewed mandate state. This base
operation does not require or enforce that choice.

","type":{"blueId":"DRxc8GkSGPbdENdB8ZK976i1Jzc6M1QdG8UsVMHcqQcf"}},"mandateTerminationChannel":{"channels":[{"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"mandateGuarantorChannel"},{"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"authorityHolderChannel"}],"description":"Composite channel through which either the guarantor or authority holder
may invoke terminateMandate. When one entry is eligible through both
members, the composite produces one logical delivery.
","type":{"blueId":"6G3SnGh7y6o8xAkphxzQAqA9btdQ2NzvKmeZzPz3JJNo"}},"terminateMandate":{"channel":{"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"mandateTerminationChannel"},"description":"Standard termination operation available to the guarantor and authority
holder.

Unless the mandate is already Mandate/Status Terminated, it emits
Mandate/Mandate Terminated with the required request reason and
correlation to the invoking Message. This includes a failed mandate,
allowing the guarantor or authority holder to stop its processing. The
operation does not write lifecycle state directly;
applyMandateTermination remains the sole authoritative termination
implementation.

On Mandate/Status Terminated it emits no lifecycle Message. Specialized
mandate types may add other operations that emit Mandate/Mandate
Terminated.

Concrete workflow steps are defined in this base type.
","request":{"reason":{"description":"Required human-readable or machine-generated termination reason.","schema":{"required":{"type":{"blueId":"AwvXD961fmnmqcSQhjMA7r15HpVh39cefb6ZTyUz2Fm2"},"value":true}},"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"}}},"steps":[{"definition":{"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"mandateLifecycleDefinition"},"entry":{"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"emitMandateTermination"},"name":"Emit Mandate Terminated","type":{"blueId":"HLwXH1Zsw9LBcFeueCCo776WxauAU8SWsHGcaarNdTab"}}],"type":{"blueId":"3zJs3fKBPAi8hRZdBrWwzdyNaAs2ZggcVfR35JWnA3ah"}}},"description":"Base executable document type for guaranteed authority delegation.

The actor bound to authorityHolderChannel controls the authority or resource
being delegated. The actor bound to authorizedActorChannel receives the
delegated authority. The actor bound to mandateGuarantorChannel confirms that
the declared authority relationship is legitimate and may terminate the
mandate.

Authority confirmation and activation are separate lifecycle facts.
Confirmation records that the guarantor accepted the authority declaration.
Activation records the timestamp from which the authorized actor may use the
delegated authority.

By default, successful authority confirmation emits Mandate/Mandate
Activated for the inherited activation workflow to apply. A mandate may set
activateOnAuthorityConfirmation to false and define an additional operation
that emits Mandate/Mandate Activated when a later condition is satisfied.

The base type defines and implements initialization, authority confirmation,
activation, termination, lifecycle event emission, lifecycle transition
guards, and graceful mandate-document termination. Subtypes inherit these
lifecycle implementations unchanged. They may add specialized fields,
validation, participants, embedded documents, and operations that emit the
standard activation or termination Messages.
","initializationError":{"description":"First deterministic initialization error when status is
Coordination/Status Failed.

Initialization writes this field only when initialization fails and stops
at the first material error rather than accumulating an error list. A
successful initialization does not write, clear, or normalize a value
already present in an authored document.
","type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"}},"name":"Mandate","status":{"description":"Current lifecycle status of the mandate.

Initialization sets exactly one initial status:

- Coordination/Status Pending when deterministic initialization succeeds.
- Coordination/Status Failed when deterministic initialization fails.

Supported transitions are:

- Coordination/Status Pending -> Mandate/Status Authority Confirmed
- Mandate/Status Authority Confirmed -> Mandate/Status Active
- Coordination/Status Pending -> Mandate/Status Terminated
- Mandate/Status Authority Confirmed -> Mandate/Status Terminated
- Mandate/Status Active -> Mandate/Status Terminated

Coordination/Status Failed and Mandate/Status Terminated are terminal.
Lifecycle workflows do not replace timestamps or statuses after the
corresponding transition succeeds.
","type":{"blueId":"6aAJEFVdFAgLVre8azY4YZQnNiv2FkXJpdpGAYSHiNrY"}},"terminatedAt":{"description":"Microsecond timestamp from which the mandate entered Mandate/Status Terminated.

The value is derived by the inherited termination workflow from the root
causal Coordination/Timeline Entry that led to the accepted
Mandate/Mandate Terminated Message. It is not supplied by that Message.
After termination succeeds, inherited lifecycle workflows do not replace
it.
","type":{"blueId":"E2LM6qgzWG9ttagq2xTmiZkgYEAgkYedFCmU9v7NnVEq"}},"validation":{"description":"Optional request-validation convention inherited by mandate subtypes.

A concrete mandate type defines which request or event is matched by
validation.request and which runtime component performs the validation.
Mandate/Operation Mandate matches the Operation Request payload.
Document-responder and MyOS mandate types may validate an entire request
Message.
","type":{"blueId":"333eCC8uWcMWgw8Ev2FfvZgJMUK9pw8LGUa1D1cYTSsQ"}}}

It divides `/contracts` changes into `add`, `modify`, and
`remove` lists so a workflow can validate and apply them coherently under Contracts Change Policy.

`add` creates new Document Section markers and their related contracts. `modify` replaces an existing section's marker
and related contracts with a full new section definition. `remove` deletes a section key and the contracts listed as
related to that section. The exact patch sequence is produced by the supporting workflow, but the semantic intent is
section-level contract evolution rather than low-level pointer editing.

This type is useful for human review, AI-agent proposal validation, and audit trails because it preserves why a set of
contract changes belong together.

{"calculationPeriodDatesReference":{"description":"A pointer style reference to the associated calculation period dates component defined elsewhere in the document.
","type":{"blueId":"5kML8V9qeDP2N3N3L173vbHKEbT1tjwLQ89bXgwhB2jf"}},"description":"A data defining:  the parameters used to generate the reset dates schedule and associated fixing dates. The reset dates are the dates on which the new index value (which is observed on the fixing date) is applied for each period and on which the interest rate hence begins to accrue.
","finalFixingDate":{"description":"This attribute is not part of the FpML ResetDate, and has been added as part of the CDM to support the credit derivatives final fixing date.
","type":{"blueId":"397tsASyRDDk2UNpFxXBdpXar7RwXd5MEejzPtRzcxB2"}},"fixingDates":{"description":"The fixing dates are the dates on which the index values are observed. The fixing dates are specified by reference to the reset date through business days offset and an associated set of financial business centers. Normally these offset calculation rules will be those specified in the ISDA definition for the relevant floating rate index (ISDA's Floating Rate Option). However, non-standard offset calculation rules may apply for a trade if mutually agreed by the principal parties to the transaction.
","type":{"blueId":"2wQPopE8rNJu4jigpcsKNP5ifSGS1mCEULs5TFyadHG9"}},"initialFixingDate":{"description":"The initial fixing date.","type":{"blueId":"FPAtrQmLwvdTAhhNkbMnaP7hvmLYgHJKT7qPEwcHqDH"}},"name":"cdm/product/common/schedule/ResetDates","rateCutOffDaysOffset":{"description":"Specifies the number of business days before the period end date when the rate cut-off date is assumed to apply. The financial business centers associated with determining the rate cut-off date are those specified in the reset dates adjustments. The rate cut-off number of days must be a negative integer (a value of zero would imply no rate cut off applies in which case the rateCutOffDaysOffset element should not be included). The relevant rate for each reset date in the period from, and including, a rate cut-off date to, but excluding, the next applicable period end date (or, in the case of the last calculation period, the termination date) will (solely for purposes of calculating the floating amount payable on the next applicable payment date) be deemed to be the relevant rate in effect on that rate cut-off date. For example, if rate cut-off days for a daily averaging deal is -2 business days, then the refix rate applied on (period end date - 2 days) will also be applied as the reset on (period end date - 1 day), i.e. the actual number of reset dates remains the same but from the rate cut-off date until the period end date, the same refix rate is applied. Note that in the case of several calculation periods contributing to a single payment, the rate cut-off is assumed only to apply to the final calculation period contributing to that payment. The day type associated with the offset must imply a business days offset.
","type":{"blueId":"GWTMGPw1zgQW3M9NUS6RxNtce5jWU9defVNkm7sV6b8L"}},"resetDatesAdjustments":{"description":"The definition of the business day convention and financial business centers used for adjusting the reset date if it would otherwise fall on a day that is not a business day in the specified business center.
","type":{"blueId":"HZJDnv878jZDzx4XhQtskoT3SAT9j2YgYkiuAfxKPXsS"}},"resetFrequency":{"description":"The frequency at which the reset dates occur. In the case of a weekly reset frequency, also specifies the day of the week that the reset occurs. If the reset frequency is greater than the calculation period frequency then this implies that more than one reset is established for each calculation period and some form of rate averaging is applicable.
","type":{"blueId":"AF5YX5ckQEQZD9m6QJzHQVPjpFFBeLnKV7o2AHf2HpW"}},"resetRelativeTo":{"description":"Specifies whether the reset dates are determined with respect to each adjusted calculation period start date or adjusted calculation period end date. If the reset frequency is specified as daily this element must not be included.
","type":{"blueId":"3ZYqtSitUczzgy8NY3j1qRo5fJi2TtUC4AfsKAq6bs3V"}}}
